guard.what: Risk guard: no second bet on the same move (correlation), total open risk capped by tail loss, daily and weekly brakes

lock.what: Profit lock: once a trade is well on its way the stop goes to break-even, and after the first target it always keeps at least half of the best open profit

trend2.what: Compass trend reader: market direction from many views that must agree (Bitcoin's 20/50/200-day trends, breadth across coins, stocks, the dollar), five states incl. sideways, smoothed so noise cannot flip it

gate.what: Trend gate: no shorts while the Compass trend reader says the market is rising. Over 7 past periods: +3.4% a month on average vs +2.0% without it, and the worst period improved from -11.9% to -2.0% a month

timestop.what: Time stop: a trade that has made no progress (under +0.5%) after 24 hours is closed instead of waiting for its stop

pace.what: Fluid pace: several trades a day when the evidence is there (learned from its own opportunity rate), Grade S always allowed

kelly.what: Edge-proportional sizing: fractional Kelly from the calibrated odds (bigger only when the edge is proven)

online-fast.what: Learns which evidence is right from every scored candidate, forgets old evidence fast (Kalman-style online learning)

online-slow.what: Same online learning, forgets slowly (more stable)

recal.what: Recalibrated odds: the raw odds are corrected by what really happened to past candidates at each odds level (learned from the live ledger; no correction until 20 separate market moves are scored)

tiers.what: Conviction tiers: a small probe (0.5% risk) when the edge is thin, standard (1-2%) with 3+ points of edge and 2 witnesses, high conviction (3-4%) with 8+ points, 3 witnesses and the market state on its side

bold.what: Bold: the same trades as the Arbiter at double the risk (8% of the account at the stop for Grade A, 4% for Grade B)

bestofday.what: Best case of the day: the bar eases gradually through the day (to half its safety margin by the last hour) when nothing better has appeared

weekpace.what: Weekly pace with carry-over: a quiet day's unused trade can be used later in the same week (up to 3 in one day)

bocpd-gate.what: Changepoint fast-track: Bayesian online changepoint detection on Bitcoin's return and market breadth; when a change is detected and the long side's graded calls since then beat their break-even over 15+ calls, longs unlock at once instead of waiting for the slow exam window

pairs.what: Pair trades: long the coin it likes most, short the one it dislikes most, among coins that move together (the market's swings cancel; tight stop even in wild markets)

runner.what: Runner: on long signals, a small first risk, then one more unit at every further +2% with the stop one step behind, held up to 14 days (rare, very large winners; most attempts lose the first risk)

news.what: News drift: after a sudden market-wide shock, ride the move in its direction on the coin whose evidence agrees most (24h limit)

flushlong.what: Flush-absorb long, bull-score gated: while the bull score is on (BTC above its 50/200-day averages, 30-day trend up, spot CVD positive, options fear calm), buy the coin whose longs were just flushed while spot buyers absorb it; full exit at +2% (lab test Nov 15: unseen 2023-26 +2.2%/month)

range.what: Range trades: in wild but sideways markets, short near the top of a coin's 3-day range and buy near the bottom (+1% target, stop just outside)

curious.what: Curious: unfamiliar situations are grouped by kind; a kind with a proven live record becomes tradable (its own witness)

curious-side.what: Curious, coarse: unfamiliar calls grouped only by side and market state; a group becomes tradable once it is right well above break-even over 20+ separate 6-hour market moves (live Nov 16: unfamiliar shorts 82/89 right, but only 15 moves in one falling week)

alloc.what: Daily-goal allocator: one budget per opportunity (up to 30% margin, 6% risk), all-in on one strong setup or split across 2-4 coins that are NOT the same bet; judged on account growth

lowbar.what: Less cautious: half the safety margin above break-even (catches over-caution live)

cointrust.what: Coin trust: demands more evidence on groups of coins where its own live odds proved too optimistic

rules.what: Research rules as fair witnesses: a rule counts only by its LIVE record in the current market state (trusted: odds up; keeps failing: a warning sign, odds down)

doubt.what: Split jury: when the witnesses disagree with each other, the bar rises by how much they disagree

roadmap:
Product: Volvox, powered by the Drosophila research engine (check trademarks and domains before going public; note the closeness to "Volvo"). Technical plan for the next build: BUILD_A.md in the repo.

Rules of the board

  • One judge. The referee makes every decision. Everything else is evidence fed into it; nothing gets its own vote or account.
  • Every idea is a challenger. A clone of the judge with exactly one change is scored on the same live cases. It takes over only if it is more accurate, finds at least as many Grade A trades and keeps its odds as honest. Most ideas are expected to fail and be dropped.
  • Subtraction too. Every build also tests the judge without each witness. Evidence that adds nothing is removed. When scores tie, the simpler version wins.
  • One scoreboard: honest odds that turn into profitable Grade A trades. Win big, lose small.
  • Fluidity. No hard-coded numbers. Every setting is learned from evidence and moves slowly.
  • Data first. New data is collected weeks before it is used, so it arrives with history.
  • Never stopped by technical limits. Free tools only, bounded storage, health checks on every limit. Paid items only from real profits.

Timeline

  • Now (paper): baseline running since Nov 7; new data recording since Nov 9
  • Wed Nov 11: Build A (foundation, honest scoring, trade shape, risk, learning, new evidence, clean-up, Volvox dashboard)
  • About 1 week after A: Build B (accuracy upgrades), once Build A has run cleanly for a few days; its challengers join the queue as test slots free up
  • At least 1 month of paper AND the gate passed: Build C (real money), earliest around mid-December
  • By April 2027: decide how the AWS server is paid for after the free credits end on May 9, 2027 (from profits, or move)

Status

  • Stage 1: referee account, about 50 coins, exams, exchange-style UI, health report
  • Stage 2: spot vs futures, Hyperliquid, self-adapting referee, live scorecard, post-mortems, monthly report
  • Own relay server (AWS Stockholm, fixed IP), with Render and Vercel as backups
  • Vercel, cron and Upstash clean-up
  • Storage can never block us: memory bounded and compressed, server compresses and deletes old files itself, health checks on disk, memory and CPU
  • Baseline: about 24 clean runs and 30 to 40 scored calls before Build A

Recording now (data only, no decisions change)

  • Own-server recorder: order-book depth every minute, live funding every 5 minutes, liquidations live (Binance's new stream address)
  • Outside world, daily: Nasdaq-100, S&P 500, VIX, US 10-year yield, dollar (FRED)
  • On-chain, daily: BTC and ETH exchange inflows, outflows and balances, active addresses (Coin Metrics)
  • Hyperliquid whales, hourly: positions of the 50 largest accounts
  • Calibration ledger: every scanned candidate with each witness's opinion and the full price path afterwards
  • News headlines, hourly: crypto, macro, geopolitics and regulation (public news feeds and Google News searches)
  • Add NVIDIA, chip index and other daily stock data (Stooq or similar) so it also has history by the time it is used — Compass global markets, Nov 11

Build A (Wed Nov 11), in build order

Built Nov 11. Waiting for data history: recorder, whale and news witnesses (auto-trained at ~21 days). Still open: measurement-level attribution, live lab (every champion in its own shadow account), state-aware research and research aimed at +2% (the research engine is the testing ground; changed last).

A1. Foundation

  • Split the referee into brain / policy / ledger / challengers
  • Challenger system: registry, promotion rule, one-click rollback, an on/off switch for every challenger. Challengers are scored on every ledger candidate (about 100 a day), not only on traded calls, so they are judged in days instead of months
  • Subtraction tests (judge without each witness)
  • Ledgers moved out of the main memory file; staggered training (at most one brain per run); run-time guard that skips training, never trading
  • Calls made in the same market move count as one bet (effective number of bets) in every score

A2. Honest scoring

  • Calibration table on the dashboard (predicted odds vs what happened), per side, market state and coin group
  • Skipped-trade review: error type of every miss (wrong read / stopped first / over- or under-confident / bar too high) from the full price path
  • Missed-winners count: what caution cost vs what it saved; if caution costs money, the judge loosens itself
  • Honest timing: paper fills at the live price at decision time, not the hour's open

A3. Trade shape, pacing and risk (policy challengers)

  • Trade shape adapts to volatility (built; FAILED its final exam on the newest months, so it is not admitted; retried after each weekly retrain): the target grows with the stop, so a wild market no longer forces an 80% bar
  • (TESTED, FAILED, not built) Best trade shape per situation (first version tested: chased +6% targets and lost on the exam; redesign later): odds for a ladder of targets (+2/+4/+8%) and horizons (4h/24h/72h); pick the highest expected profit; learned runner targets and trail width — retried with volatility-scaled targets after each retrain; fails its exam
  • Fluid pacing: learned trade pace (no fixed 1 a day or 7 a week), several trades a day allowed, weekly pace by count and profit, surplus carries over, new top tier Grade S
  • Fluid risk: total open-risk cap, same-bet (correlation) guard, daily and weekly brakes
  • Edge-proportional sizing: fractional Kelly from calibrated odds, bigger only when the edge is proven

A4. Learning which evidence was right

  • Every scored candidate, traded or skipped, adjusts how much each witness is trusted, per market state (recursive, Kalman-style online learning with a forgetting factor; the forgetting speed itself is chosen by competing challengers)
  • Inside each witness (witness-level 'which one misled' is live; measurement-level needs the raw values stored, next): which measurement pushed the odds the wrong way; misleading measurements are down-weighted, and missing ones become research targets — measurement drift monitor live Nov 12: flags measurements whose live relationship is opposite to what the brain learned
  • Coin-specific trust: the judge learns its record per coin and coin group and demands more evidence where it is weak

A5. New evidence (each one a separate challenger witness)

  • (WAITING FOR DATA) Recorder witness: liquidation bursts, order-book imbalance, live funding and premium — auto-trained at ~21 days of recordings (early December)
  • Outside-world witness: risk-on/off state from stocks, VIX, dollar and yields; macro calendar (Fed, CPI, jobs) with no new trades just before
  • (WAITING FOR DATA) Whale witness (Hyperliquid's largest accounts) — auto-trained at ~21 days
  • On-chain witness (exchange flows; stablecoin flows per chain from DefiLlama)
  • Sectors (AI, memes, L1, DeFi, exchange tokens) and sector rotation
  • (WAITING FOR DATA) News witness: headlines tagged by the AI (type, who, severity) plus a memory of similar past events; tested last, because it is the noisiest — headlines recorded hourly; AI digest and risk mood recorded 4x a day from Nov 12; witness once ~21 days exist
  • Shock memory: every past sudden move (BTC and Nasdaq since 2020, found from prices, the cause labelled from news where possible), split by bull/bear state, scheduled (Fed, CPI) vs surprise, and whether it was already priced in (drift before). It records how fast the reaction came (minutes / hours / at the next stock-market open) and whether it lasted or faded within 4h, 24h and 72h
  • Shock response for open trades (challenger): when a shock hits against an open trade, the shock memory decides exit / take profit / hold, based on what similar shocks did. This is the only case where an open trade is re-judged
  • Shock detector on the own server: records every minute-level shock with the market's reaction
  • Server guard (speed): each hourly run hands the own server the open trades plus a ready-made plan ("if a shock of this size hits against this trade: exit / take profit / hold"); the server watches every minute and acts on paper within about a minute, without waiting for the next hourly run. GitHub does the thinking, the server does the reacting

A6. Rules feed the judge

  • Account clean-up: remove the team and all-in accounts; keep the best-rule account as the testing ground
  • Live lab: every champion rule paper-traded in shadow; the best-rule account picks its champion per market state by live record (no dip-buy longs in a falling market unless they have proven themselves there) — each rule's live record per market state is tracked on every scored candidate (rule trust); the best-rule account skips rules failing in the current state
  • Highest standard for rules reaching the judge: a rule's vote counts only in the market states where its live and after-discovery record is good; a rule that keeps failing in a state becomes a warning sign there (its firing counts against its own side); rules that add nothing in the subtraction test are not fed at all
  • Research looks for rules that know the market state (a rule can include "only in a falling, wild market"), so rules are specialists instead of islands — the trend reading is now a measurement (p_mtrend) that research rules can condition on, Nov 12
  • Rules as fair witnesses (votes count only after their discovery date); rules propose and the judge approves; market sensor (which rule styles win now)
  • Research aimed at the goal: favour rules whose wins are at least +2%; curiosity-driven research pointed at the judge's blind spots

A7. Dashboard

  • Volvox branding (research engine shown as Drosophila); Overview opens on the referee; research moves to its own section
  • Upgrade-under-test panel, calibration table, Grade A pace, recorder and server status

A8. Test and deploy

  • Local end-to-end run on real data (memory and time), a 10-day replay through the whole policy, phone and desktop screenshots
  • Crash rehearsal: replay March 2020, LUNA, FTX and recent shocks through sizing and exits
  • Deploy once, watch the first 3 runs, then the daily health reports
  • Leverage per trade up to 20x (liquidation always at least 2.5x the stop away; wild coins get less), Nov 11

Next pass (from your Nov 11 notes): aim for the daily percentage, not a trade count

  • Daily-goal allocator (challenger, live Nov 11): one margin budget per opportunity window (learned, up to ~30% of the account inside the hard safety limits), spent either on ONE strong trade (and let it run) or split across 2-4 coins when several good-but-smaller edges appear at once; split only across trades that are NOT the same bet (correlation-aware: four shorts on coins that move together count as one trade). Judged on account growth (compounding), not number of trades
  • (TESTED, FAILED, not built) Smaller targets when that is where the edge is (challenger): +1% / +1.5% targets allowed when their odds are high enough to pay after fees (two +1% trades = one +2% day) — +0.8 / +1 / +1.5% all worse than +2% over 7 past periods
  • Opportunity-sized risk: Grade S + Kelly + allocator together: much bigger when the evidence is strong and proven, small or none when it is not — Grade S, Kelly and allocator challengers are live and scored
  • Never too cautious by design (lower-bar challenger live Nov 11): promotions already require at least as many Grade A trades and at least as much profit (a "safer but idle" upgrade cannot win); missed-winners count loosens the bar when caution costs money; a challenger with a LOWER bar runs alongside so over-caution is caught live

Audit, Nov 11 (what the evidence says about the goal)

  • Promotions need proof (a consistent lead over 40+ separate 6-hour windows and 10+ days); self-adjustment counts separate market moves, not correlated calls
  • A bar per trend state (challenger, live Nov 11): on the newest four months it took ~2.6x the trades with a higher win rate (local test: 3.7 trades/week, +10.3%/month vs 1.4 and +2.3% for the single bar; deeper worst drop 22% vs 8%). Longs return only in rising and sideways markets
  • Pullback entries: tested, failed (missed more than half the trades, no better quality); not built
  • Walk-forward audit (7 past periods, Nov 11): shorts positive in 5 of 7, about +2% a month on average as the exam scores them (about +0.8% as traded); lost 12% a month in the 2025 rally. Longs about zero. The Nov 7 brain no longer matched the data: retrained early
  • Pyramiding lab test (Nov 11): fails on shorts (the Arbiter's short signals are quick small drops, only 3% became 20% moves); passes on longs through rare very large winners -> runner challenger (live Nov 11)
  • New approaches tested overnight Nov 11-12, walk-forward over past periods, none passed: (1) learned cross-sectional ranking, long top / short bottom coins, 24h and 72h: about -0.6% a month on average, rank correlation near zero; (2) screened composite of the reliable measurements: negative in most periods; (3) short-horizon ranking (4h / 8h): a small edge before costs (about 0.02-0.08% per trade) that fees erase; (4) learned phase judge (market up or down over 7 / 14 days): 52% accuracy, a coin flip, also when confident. Conclusion: with the current free hourly data there is no large hidden edge; the Arbiter's short edge remains the best evidence found
  • Trend-gate test (7 past periods, Nov 12): shorts switched off while the trend reader says "up" averaged +3.4% a month vs +2.0%, with the worst period cut from -11.9% to -2.0% and smaller drops in every period -> trend gate challenger (live Nov 12). Longs restricted to rising markets still lost slightly (-0.5% a month); smaller short targets (+0.8 / +1 / +1.5%) were worse than +2%; neither built
  • Honest status of the goal: evidence supports ~1-4 good trades a week; lowering the bar to trade daily lost money in the test. More good trades must come from better evidence (trend reader, Compass, long-side edge), not from a lower bar

NEXT (top priority): an accurate trend reader, shared by every part

Today the market state comes from ONE measure (BTC above/below its 50-day average, plus volatility): slow to turn, and it can flip on noise.

  • Several views that must agree: BTC vs its 20/50/200-day averages and their slopes, 7- and 30-day moves, breadth (share of coins below their own averages, new lows vs new highs), funding and open interest across coins, Nasdaq trend
  • Five states with a confidence: strong down / down / sideways / up / strong up (sideways is real and matters)
  • Turn detection (change points) so a real reversal is caught early, and hysteresis so noise does not flip it back and forth — 12-hour smoothing prevents flips; a learned change-point model was tested as the phase judge and failed (coin flip)
  • Measured honestly: how often each state correctly called the next 1, 3 and 7 days, shown on the dashboard
  • ONE trend reading feeds everything (the Arbiter, every challenger and specialist, the best-rule account), so no part can disagree with another about the market; enters as a challenger against today's reader — one column (p_mtrend) feeds the trend-reader challenger, the trend gate, the state plans and research; the Arbiter switches to it only by promotion

NEXT, together with the trend reader: "Compass", a market-intelligence engine feeding the Arbiter

Bitcoin alone is ~20% of the picture. Compass reads the whole world every hour and hands the Arbiter (and the trend reader) evidence, never decisions.

  • Global markets (long free history, trainable now): S&P 500, Nasdaq, Dow, Europe (DAX, FTSE), Asia (Nikkei, Hang Seng), dollar index, gold, oil, US 2y/10y yields, VIX; NVIDIA and chip stocks; crypto vs each (who leads whom, how tight the link is right now)
  • Money flows: Bitcoin / Ethereum ETF daily flows (history since Jan 2024), stablecoin supply (DefiLlama), exchange flows (Coin Metrics, recording) — stablecoin supply (DefiLlama, since 2017) and exchange flows live Nov 12 as the money-flow witness; ETF flows: no free machine-readable source found yet
  • Mood: Fear & Greed index (history since 2018), funding and positioning across coins, options mood (Deribit, recording from now) — Fear & Greed plus the options fear gauge (Deribit implied volatility, since 2021), Nov 12
  • Calendar: Fed, CPI, jobs (economic calendar feed), big earnings (NVIDIA...), IPOs (Nasdaq IPO calendar), token unlocks; the Arbiter knows what is coming and how similar events moved crypto before — economic calendar and IPO calendar live; earnings dates and token unlocks not yet
  • News digest: headlines from Reuters / Bloomberg / CNBC / Yahoo Finance / MarketWatch / CoinDesk / The Block via public feeds; the AI tags each (type, assets, sectors such as AI coins, direction, severity) and writes a short daily market brief on the dashboard — AI brief, risk mood and tagged events 4x a day on the Overview, Nov 12
  • Event memory: every tagged event stored with what crypto and each sector did after 1h / 1d / 1w (e.g. how AI coins moved around big AI news and AI IPOs), so a new event is judged by what similar ones did
  • Event playbooks: for every known upcoming event (weeks ahead), Compass builds a plan from past events of the same family: which coins are affected (e.g. AI coins TAO, FET, NEAR, WLD for AI news / AI IPOs), what happened before / on / after the day (run-up, "sell the news" or "buy the news"), how often and how big. The Arbiter turns it into conditional plans (e.g. "if TAO dips 5% in the 2 days before, consider a long"), traded only when the playbook has enough past cases and its own evidence agrees; every plan is paper-traded and scored, so playbooks earn trust like everything else. Event families with history in our data: crypto-company listings (Coinbase Apr 2021, Circle Jun 2025), big AI moments (ChatGPT Nov 2022), NVIDIA earnings (~20), Fed / CPI days (~100)
  • Each Compass input enters as a witness challenger (no noise allowed in); the global-risk state also feeds the trend reader

Wild-market specialists (from your Nov 11 notes; each a challenger, used only when the Arbiter judges the odds good)

  • Profit lock (live Nov 11): break-even once a trade is well on its way; after the first target it keeps at least half of the best open profit
  • Curious about unfamiliar situations (live Nov 11): every unfamiliar candidate is recorded and scored, grouped by kind; a kind with a proven record becomes tradable, a failing kind is avoided, a mixed kind stays "it is what it is"
